summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses the halakhic implications of cancelling a verbal business agreement, specifically focusing on a scenario where a catering order is cancelled shortly before the event. He explores the concepts of trustworthiness, the obligation to mitigate losses, and how the distribution of profit and expenses is handled when a cancelled order is resold to another party.
questions: Is a verbal agreement binding in business?
What is the rabbinical curse of Mishapara?
Does a person who cancels an order have to pay for the full cost if the business owner can resell the items?
What happens if a business owner makes more profit by reselling a cancelled order than they would have made originally?
